Nina —

Appreciate the quick follow. Short answers up front: we can do either consolidated invoicing or entity-specific invoices, but each option has tradeoffs on accounting and tax paperwork. Below I summarized options and next steps so procurement/legal can decide which fits your finance processes.

Option A — Consolidated invoice to LaunchPad, Inc. (US):
- Redwood issues a single invoice to LaunchPad, Inc.
- We include line-item breakdowns by region and currency.
- For EU usage, LaunchPad confirms reverse-charge applicability; Redwood will include a VAT note but would typically expect LaunchPad to self-account for VAT under reverse charge (we do not gross up by default).
- If LaunchPad requires Redwood to gross up or accept withholding responsibility, that needs explicit contract language and is subject to tax/economic approval.

Option B — Entity-specific invoicing per Redwood billing entity:
- Separate invoices routed to the paying entity for the region (e.g., Redwood EU invoiced to LaunchPad EU entity).
- Cleaner from a VAT compliance standpoint; avoids need for gross-up clauses.
- May require separate POs/invoice recipients on your side.

Operational asks from us to finalize:
1) Confirm which invoice path you prefer.
2) Confirm net terms (we usually propose net 30 for self-serve, net 45 for committed/bespoke deals) — if LaunchPad needs net 60 or backdated terms, we may need credit approval.
3) If you want Redwood to accept reverse-charge language as-is, let us know which specific clause you want in the order form; legal will need to redline the MSA (clause references please).

I attached a redline template (AF_OrderForm_redline.docx) that Kimberly and Ben will update for your preferred path. If convenient, I can schedule a 30-minute call between LaunchPad procurement, Redwood finance (Kimberly), and legal next day to lock this.

Next step suggestion: confirm invoice routing and net terms now; we’ll circulate a redline to your legal team by EOD.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Hi all —

Adding finance detail so procurement has the implications:

If LaunchPad chooses consolidated invoicing to LaunchPad, Inc.:
- Redwood can issue consolidated invoices but we require a billing contact and a single PO reference per invoice.
- For EU VAT, LaunchPad needs to confirm VAT registration numbers for the entities consuming the service and provide a VAT self-assessment statement if applying reverse-charge.
- Redwood does not agree to gross-up or absorb withholding by default. If LaunchPad requests language that shifts VAT/withholding to Redwood, we need a commercial concession or an offset in pricing (we can discuss a limited grooming credit).

If LaunchPad prefers entity-specific invoices:
- We will map each invoice to the indicated entity; please share the remit-to name, tax ID, and preferred currency for each.

Net terms:
- For this order form/commit level we can accept net 45 as a standard for committed deals. Net 30 is possible for smaller commitments. Net 60 would need credit review (adds ~7–10 business days).

Attachments: pricing-breakdown.xlsx — shows how we would present line items by region and the impact of a 2% gross-up on unit price if Redwood were to absorb withholding.

Legal ask (to Alex/legal):
- If LaunchPad insists on reverse-charge indemnity language, we need Legal to redline section 6.2 (Tax and Withholding) of the MSA to clarify gross-up treatment and auditing rights. Ben, can you /legal take?

If helpful, I’ve penciled in a 30-min slot tomorrow at 10am PT for a quick ops/legal sync; otherwise we’ll proceed by redline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
